errors.catalogo.notPublic: This item is not public, or the link no longer exists. On archive.org an item can also exist but have restricted access: then you can listen on the site but not take it away.
errors.catalogo.resolveFailed: This link could not be read. Open «Why doesn't it work?» below to see where it stopped.
errors.catalogo.listTruncated: The catalog sent fewer tracks than it claims, and this playlist already exists: replacing it now would lose the missing ones. Try again shortly.
errors.catalogo.notAvailable: This catalog is not responding. The others keep working: the queue will skip whatever only it had.
errors.db.openFailed: The library database will not open. Check that the data folder exists and is writable; its path is in Settings, under «Library and data».
errors.db.queryFailed: The database refused a request. The cases that depend on your computer — a read-only database, a drive that fails a read, a data folder on the network, a database that is busy — each have a message of their own: if you are reading this one, the fault is almost always Aether's. Restarting sometimes gets around it; if it comes back at the same point every time, it is worth reporting.
errors.db.migrationFailed: The database upgrade did not complete, and nothing was written halfway. The previous database is intact: restart, and if the error returns keep a copy of the data folder.
errors.db.corrupt: The library database is damaged. If you have a Drive backup, restore it from Settings; otherwise a new scan rebuilds the library, but not play counts and ratings.
errors.db.locked: The database is busy with another operation. Wait for it to finish — usually a scan — and try again.
errors.db.readOnly: The library database is read-only, so Aether can't save anything to it. Check the permissions on the data folder — the path is in Settings, under «Library and data» — and that the drive isn't write-protected.
errors.db.networkPath: Aether's data folder is on a network share, or the network stopped answering while it was in use. The database doesn't work properly there: Aether carries on, but the interface stalls during a scan. This usually happens when the Windows user folder is redirected to the network. The path is shown in Settings › Library and data; Aether can't move it by itself yet.
errors.db.ioFailed: The drive refused a read on the database. This isn't a bad request, it's the hardware. Make a copy of the data folder now, before asking that drive for anything else.
errors.db.versionAhead: This database was written by a newer version of Aether, and opening it with this one would damage it. Update the application.
errors.download.unrecognizedUrl: This link is not from a catalog Aether can take music from. «archive.org» and «audius.co» both work.
errors.download.invalidUrl: This address cannot be read. Copy it again from the browser bar: a piece often gets lost when typing it by hand.
errors.download.notPermitted: This track can be listened to but not copied: its license does not allow it. You will find it under «To buy», with links to get it where the artist is paid.
errors.download.noResults: No free catalog has this track. That does not mean it does not exist: it means it exists nowhere it would be lawful to take it from. It went to «To buy».
errors.download.private: This item is private. Only whoever uploaded it can see it.
errors.download.unavailable: This item is no longer at its address. Search for the track by name: the same piece is often somewhere else too.
errors.download.forbidden: The catalog refused the request. This happens after many downloads in a row: wait a few minutes and try again.
errors.download.rateLimited: Too many requests in a row: the catalog asked to slow down. It resumes by itself shortly.
errors.download.rateLimitedRetry: The catalog asked to wait. Aether retries by itself: there is nothing to redo.
errors.download.network: The connection dropped during the download. What had arrived is not lost: try again when the network is back.
errors.download.badResponse: The catalog replied with something Aether cannot read. If it is a fault on their side it passes by itself; if it stays, report it.
errors.download.invalidFiles: The files that arrived are not readable audio. The item may hold only images or text: look at it on the catalog's site.
errors.download.externalSearchFailed: The search across the catalogs failed. Try again, or paste the page link directly.
errors.download.failed: The download failed. Try again: if it happens again, the technical detail is under «Why doesn't it work?».
errors.fs.notFound: This file is no longer where it was. It may have been moved outside Aether: a scan puts the library back in order.
errors.fs.permissionDenied: Aether does not have permission to read or write here. Pick a folder of your own, or change this one's permissions.
errors.fs.pathInvalid: This path cannot be used. Pick a folder that exists and that you are allowed to write to.
errors.fs.diskFull: The disk is full. Free some space and try again: nothing was written halfway.
errors.fs.inUse: This file is open in another program. Close it and try again.
errors.fs.trashFailed: This file could not go to the Recycle Bin. It may be open in another program, or sit on a drive that has no Recycle Bin — a USB stick, a network folder: there Windows would just delete it, and Aether will not do that for you.
errors.fs.readFailed: This file could not be read. If it is on an external drive or a network folder, check that it is still connected.
errors.fs.writeFailed: Writing to disk failed. Check the free space and the folder's permissions.
errors.fs.networkUnavailable: The network folder is not responding: the server may be off, the VPN down, the cable unplugged. No tracks are lost and the library was left untouched — try again when the network is back.
errors.ia.notConfigured: No model is configured. The Studio chat talks to nobody until you add one under Settings › AI Models.
errors.ia.unauthorized: The provider rejected the key. Write it again under Settings › AI Models: that is the only thing this error asks for, and a revoked key does not come back on its own.
errors.ia.modelUnknown: This provider does not know that model. Read the list again with the button that tests the connection: the names change more often than you would think.
errors.ia.badResponse: The service claims to speak like OpenAI, and does not. If the address is yours, check that it answers on /v1; if it is a known provider, the fault is on their side and passes by itself.
errors.ia.notLoopback: This address is not encrypted and is not this computer: the request would leave in the clear, readable by anyone in between. Use https://, or a service running right here — localhost.
errors.ia.localServerDown: The local model is not answering. It is not the network: it is Ollama or LM Studio that is not running, or is listening on another port. Start it and try again.
errors.ia.busy: There is already a conversation running. Wait for it to finish, or stop it: one at a time, otherwise two answers would write over each other on the same document.
errors.ia.noAnswer: The service accepted the request and closed without answering. It happens on free models, when the provider's queue expires before your turn: try again, or pick a less crowded model.
errors.internal.unexpected: Something went wrong in a way that was not foreseen. Restart Aether; if it happens again, the detail below is what to report.
errors.internal.notImplemented: This part has not been written yet. It is not a fault: it is a feature that comes later.
errors.internal.invariantViolated: Aether found itself in a state that should not exist, and stopped instead of carrying on blindly. Restart.
errors.internal.timeout: The operation took too long and stopped. On a very large library, simply trying again can be enough.
errors.internal.aborted: The operation was interrupted. Nothing was left half done.
errors.ipc.backendUnreachable: The window cannot reach Aether's core. Restart the application.
errors.ipc.handlerMissing: The window asked for something this core does not know. That happens when window and core come from different versions: reinstall Aether.
errors.ipc.payloadInvalid: The window sent the core something that does not add up. It is a defect in Aether, not yours: worth reporting.
errors.library.trackNotFound: This track is no longer in the library. A scan may have removed it because the file is gone.
errors.library.playlistExists: There is already a playlist with this name. Pick another, or rename the earlier one.
errors.library.playlistNameInvalid: This name identifies no playlist: it needs at least one letter or one digit.
errors.library.playlistIsSmart: This playlist is automatic: its rules decide what is in it, and rows added by hand would vanish at the first recalculation.
errors.library.smartRulesInvalid: These rules cannot be applied as they are. Check that every row has a field, a comparison and a value.
errors.library.smartFieldInvalid: One of the rules names a field that does not exist. Pick the field again from the list.
errors.library.smartOpInvalid: One of the rules uses a comparison that field does not accept — «contains» on a number, for instance.
errors.library.scanFailed: The scan stopped. The folders already read are kept: try again, and if it always stops at the same point look at that path.
errors.library.scanBusy: A scan is already running: wait for it to finish. If you have just downloaded something, it is the automatic scan doing the same work.
errors.metadata.tagReadFailed: This file's tags cannot be read. The file still plays, but title and artist stay as they are in the file name.
errors.metadata.tagWriteFailed: The tags of this file could not be rewritten. Check that it is not read-only and not open elsewhere.
errors.metadata.tagVerifyFailed: The tags were written but reading them back does not match, so Aether put the previous ones back. The file is as you left it.
errors.metadata.musicbrainzUnavailable: MusicBrainz is not responding. Enrichment resumes by itself on the next pass.
errors.metadata.fingerprintUnavailable: Acoustic fingerprinting is not available on this computer, so recognition relies on the existing tags alone.
errors.metadata.enrichNoMatch: No confident match for this track. It stays as it is: enrichment does not guess.
errors.metadata.enrichNeedsReview: There is a match, but not confident enough to be written on its own. Look at it yourself and decide.
errors.metadata.enrichBusy: An enrichment pass is already running. Wait for it to finish.
errors.metadata.lyricsNoMatch: The catalog does not have the lyrics for this track.
errors.metadata.lyricsPublishRefused: The lyrics were not given back to the catalog.
errors.net.hostUnknown: This address does not resolve: either the name is misspelled, or DNS is not answering. Check the address and try again.
errors.net.timeout: The server did not answer in time. Try again.
errors.net.rateLimited: Too many requests in a row: the service asked to slow down. Wait a minute and try again.
errors.net.http: The server replied with an error.
errors.net.badSchema: The service's reply does not have the expected shape. If it stays this way, something changed on their side.
errors.net.circuitOpen: This service failed too many times in a row, and Aether stopped insisting for a while. It resumes by itself.
errors.playback.engineUnavailable: The audio engine did not start. Check that the computer has an active sound card, then restart Aether.
errors.playback.deviceLost: The audio device disappeared — headphones unplugged, or the card changed. Aether looks for another one by itself; if it finds none, try again once you plug one back in.
errors.playback.formatUnsupported: This format cannot be played. The file stays in the library: converting it to FLAC or MP3 makes it playable.
errors.playback.decodeFailed: This file is damaged and cannot be decoded. If you have another copy, replace it and scan again.
errors.playback.sourceUnavailable: This track's file cannot be reached. If it is on an external drive, plug it back in.
errors.playback.stalled: Playback stalled. If the file lives on a network folder, the disk may have gone to sleep.
errors.playback.autoplayBlocked: Automatic playback was blocked. Press play once by hand.
errors.settings.corrupt: A setting is written in a way that cannot be read, and Aether fell back to the starting value instead of stopping.
errors.settings.secretUnavailable: The system keyring is not responding, so the saved credentials cannot be read. On Linux an active secret service is required.
errors.settings.lastfmNotConfigured: Last.fm is not connected yet. Connect it from Settings, under «Scrobbling».
errors.settings.lastfmNoPendingToken: There is no authorization waiting to be confirmed. Start the connection again from the beginning.
errors.settings.listenbrainzNotConfigure: ListenBrainz is not connected yet. Paste your token in Settings, under «Scrobbling».
errors.settings.scrobbleAuthRejected: The service rejected the credentials. Reconnect the account: this happens when the password has changed.
errors.settings.scrobbleRejected: The service rejected this listen. The others keep going out normally.
errors.skin.manifestInvalid: This skin's manifest cannot be read. Open it in the Studio: the problems are listed line by line.
errors.skin.packageCorrupt: This package will not open as an archive: it may have been downloaded halfway. Download it again.
errors.skin.formatUnsupported: This package is in a format Aether does not read. An «.aethskin» file is what is needed.
errors.skin.idConflict: There is already a skin with this identifier. Uninstall the earlier one, or change the identifier in the manifest.
errors.skin.builtinReadOnly: Built-in skins cannot be changed or deleted. Derive from it: the copy is yours and can be edited.
errors.skin.tokenInvalid: A token in this skin has a value that cannot be used. The Studio says which one, and where.
errors.skin.layoutIncomplete: This skin does not declare every zone needed to draw the window. The Studio lists which ones are missing.
errors.skin.unknownEffect: This skin asks for an effect this version of Aether does not know. Update the application.
errors.skin.assetRejected: A file inside this skin was rejected: skins may contain only images, fonts and text.
errors.skin.tooLarge: This package is too large. Skins stay under the limit because a skin is not a photo album.
errors.spotify.archiveUnreadable: This file will not open as an archive: it may have been downloaded halfway. Download it again from Spotify.
errors.spotify.archiveEmpty: The archive opens but holds nothing Aether can read. Spotify sends more than one: look for the one containing «Playlist1.json» or «Streaming_History_Audio».
errors.spotify.tracklistTruncated: The archive holds fewer tracks than it claims, and this playlist already exists: replacing it now would lose the missing ones. Download the archive from Spotify again.
errors.sync.busy: A synchronization is already running. Wait for it to finish: there is no need to redo it.
errors.sync.authExpired: The connection with Google is no longer valid. Reconnect the account in the Backup section, or synchronize to a shared folder instead.
errors.sync.remoteCorrupt: Another device's document cannot be read. The others keep synchronizing anyway; if the problem stays, forget that device and pair it again.
errors.sync.conflict: Two devices wrote something that could not be reconciled. Nothing was lost: synchronize again.
errors.transfer.peerNotPaired: This device is not paired. Pair it from Settings, under «Sync between devices».
errors.transfer.peerUnreachable: The other device is not answering. Check that it is on and on the same network.
errors.transfer.pairingExpired: The pairing code has expired. Ask for a new one: they last a few minutes on purpose.
errors.transfer.pairingRateLimited: Too many pairing attempts. Wait a few minutes before trying again.
errors.transfer.pinInvalid: This code is not the right one. Read it again on the other device.
errors.transfer.sessionBusy: A transfer with this device is already running. Wait for it to finish.
errors.transfer.methodNotSupported: This device cannot do this kind of transfer. Update Aether on both.
errors.transfer.integrityMismatch: What arrived does not match what was sent, so it was discarded. Try again.
errors.transfer.aborted: The transfer was interrupted. Nothing was left half done.
rules.intro: A smart playlist does not hold tracks: it holds a question. Its contents are the library filtered {adesso}, and they change by themselves when you add music or listen to something — with nobody touching it.
rules.name: Name
rules.takesAll: No conditions: this playlist would hold {tutta}. That is a legitimate result and almost never the intended one.
rules.takesNothing: «At least one holds» with no conditions is never true: this playlist would stay empty forever.
rules.incomplete: A condition without a value does not count yet: write what to look for and the number above updates.
rules.skipped: {n} conditions do not stand up and were skipped: that happens when the field and the operator disagree — «year» with «contains», for instance.
rules.skipped.uno: One condition does not stand up and was skipped: that happens when the field and the operator disagree — «year» with «contains», for instance.

delete.library.title: Remove {brani} from the library?
delete.library.body: The rating, the like, the play counts and the place in playlists go away with the row. The files stay where they are: if they are still inside a watched folder, the next scan puts them back — without any of that. To not see them again, use “Delete from disk…”.
delete.disk.title: Delete {brani} from disk?
delete.disk.body: The files go to the Recycle Bin, and the library loses the rating, the like, the play counts and the place in playlists. You can get them back from the Recycle Bin, but Aether will not notice on its own: once they are back in place, use “Scan”.
delete.done.back: Out of the library: {brani}. {n} of them come back at the next scan: their files are still in a watched folder.
delete.done.back.uno: Out of the library: {brani}. One will come back at the next scan: its file is still in a watched folder.

tour.step.benvenuto.title: Welcome to Aether
tour.step.benvenuto.body: Aether plays the music on your computer: it reads it from the folders you choose, keeps it in order without rewriting your files, and finds lyrics and covers for it. In ten steps it shows you where everything is.
tour.step.navigazione.title: This is where you go from
tour.step.navigazione.body: The left bar holds destinations only: Home, Albums, Artists, Tracks, Folders, Favourites. The button at the top narrows it to icons when you need the room.
tour.step.ricerca.title: Searching
tour.step.ricerca.body: The field at the top searches the whole library as you type, from any screen. The «/» key puts the cursor there without touching the mouse.
tour.step.riga-brano.title: A track row
tour.step.riga-brano.body: A double click starts the list from here, not the single track: after the third comes the fourth. Right click opens the menu with everything you can do to a track.
tour.step.trasporto.title: Controls and slider
tour.step.trasporto.body: Play, previous and next, shuffle and repeat. The slider beside them says where you are and can be dragged: the time on the left is the position, the one on the right the length.
tour.step.giudizio.title: Heart, stars, and what the file is
tour.step.giudizio.body: The heart adds to favourites, the stars give a one-to-five rating. Below them the technical line — format, sample rate, channels, kbps — says which edition you are listening to.
tour.step.colonna.title: The column, and the queue
tour.step.colonna.body: The right-hand column tells you what is playing and what comes next. It can be closed, and once closed the queue reopens from the button in the player bar.
tour.step.in-riproduzione.title: Full screen
tour.step.in-riproduzione.body: Cover art, synced lyrics and the spectrum analyser in one place. Lyric lines can be clicked to jump, and the offset strip brings a lyric that drifts back into step.
tour.step.playlist.title: Playlists
tour.step.playlist.body: Yours live here. The three buttons next to the heading make a new one, make one that updates itself from rules, or bring one in from a file.
tour.step.studio.title: The skin Studio
tour.step.studio.body: A skin repaints the whole window, the visualizer's scene included. The Studio is the editor built into Aether for making one, and «Create theme» is the way in.
tour.step.impostazioni.title: Everything else
tour.step.impostazioni.body: Watched folders, audio output, equalizer, services, updates. The keyboard shortcuts can be read and changed under «Motion and access».
page.playlist.smart.note: This is an automatic playlist: it holds no tracks, it holds a question. What you see is the library filtered {adesso}, and it changes by itself when you add music or listen to something. For the same reason it cannot be edited by hand: you change the rules, with a right click on its name.

settings.roots.note: Aether reads; it neither moves nor changes

settings.roots.empty: No folders. Aether does not know yet where you keep your music.
settings.scan.note: An interrupted scan leaves a library that is correct and incomplete: every batch sits in its own transaction, and the next pass picks up where this one stopped.
settings.scan.result: {inseriti} added · {aggiornati} updated · {spostati} moved · {tolti} removed, in {secondi} s
settings.scan.stopped.rest: : a new scan resumes from here without rereading what is already there.
settings.scan.skipped.rest: : the tracks inside were left alone, not removed. Reconnect the drive or the network and scan again.
settings.scan.held.rest: : too many tracks were disappearing at once for it to be intentional, and nothing was removed. If that really is what happened, scan again.
settings.downloads.title: Where downloaded tracks land
settings.downloads.note: When an import finds a track you do not have, the queue goes and fetches it and writes it here. By default that is the {prima}, and it is not a convenient fallback: a file downloaded outside those folders is a file no scan ever finds — that is, a successful download that never appears in the library, indistinguishable from a failed one.
settings.downloads.needRoot: A watched folder is needed first: without one there is nowhere a download could land and still be found.
settings.downloads.outside: This folder is not inside any of the watched ones: tracks will arrive there, but they will not appear in the library until you add it to the folders above.
sync.lines.help: One line per verse. Blank lines in between stay: they are the pauses between verses, and they have a time too.
sync.elsewhere: Another track is playing: taps are on hold until you go back to this one.
sync.tap.help: Start the track and press Space at the beginning of each line. Do not worry about the lag: it corrects itself.
sync.tap.done: That is all of them. Press «Straighten» and the core snaps your taps to the track's real onsets.
sync.tap.key: Space to tap · ⌫ to redo the last one · Enter when you are done
sync.done.savedInLibrary: Saved in Aether, but not next to the track: other players won't see it.
sync.done.offer: If you like, this work can go back to LRCLIB, the open catalog the other lyrics come from. Whoever has the same song will not have to do it again.
sync.done.slow: It takes a few seconds, and not because of the network: the catalog asks for a bit of computation on every submission, and that is how it keeps out whoever would fill it with junk.
sync.done.thanks: Sent. Thank you: the next person will find it already done.
sync.review.help: The times are snapped to the track's onsets and corrected for your reaction lag. Nudge the ones that are off.
sync.review.where: It lands in an .lrc file next to the track, which other players read too. The audio bytes are never touched.
sync.words.help: Start the track again and press Space at the beginning of each word. Single-word lines aren't listed: their time is already known.
sync.words.done: That's all of them. “Straighten” snaps these to the track's real onsets too; then touch up what needs it and save.
sync.words.key: Space to tap a word · ⌫ to redo the last one · Enter when you're done
sync.words.where: Word timings go into an .a2.lrc file next to the track, and the usual .lrc stays there for players that don't know what an a2 is.
sync.words.attached: {n} lines also carry word timings: an .a2.lrc file goes next to the track too.
sync.words.attached.uno: One line also carries word timings: an .a2.lrc file goes next to the track too.
settings.lyrics.title: Lyrics
settings.lyrics.note: Where they come from, and how many are missing
settings.lyrics.p1: Aether looks at what you already have first: an .lrc file next to the track, or the lyrics inside the tag. When there is neither, it asks LRCLIB — a public, key-free catalogue built by the people who use it.
settings.lyrics.p2: Requests {mai} go out on their own in the background: only for the track you are playing, and only while the lyrics panel is open. The fill below is the one pass over your whole library, and you start it.
settings.lyrics.toggle.hint: Off, only the lyrics already in your files are used
settings.lyrics.pace: Four requests per second, no more: the catalogue hosts us for free and does not defend itself. A thousand tracks take a few minutes.
settings.enrich.title: Metadata
settings.enrich.note: Kept in the database, and never touches your files
settings.enrich.p1: When a track comes in with no album, no cover, or a title taken from a catalog, Aether looks the record up on MusicBrainz and writes what it finds into its own library — not into your files, which stay exactly as they were. It looks for {album}, not the single track: twelve lengths that match are proof, a title that resembles another is not.
settings.enrich.p2: When the evidence is not enough it {niente} and tries again later. That is why there is no screen to approve: uncertain matches are discarded rather than queued up for somebody.
settings.enrich.toggle: Enrich the metadata on its own
settings.enrich.toggle.hint: One pass every half hour, and after every scan or download. Nothing it finds goes into your files: forget it whenever you like, with one click.
settings.enrich.pace: One record at a time, with a pause between requests: MusicBrainz allows one per second, and that is why it looks up the album and not the individual tracks.
settings.enrich.result: Last pass: {applicati} applied · {astenuti} left alone ({senza} of them with no match)
settings.enrich.undo.note: Forgetting reads the tags back from your files — which are untouched — and {spegne}: without that, the next pass would put back within half an hour what you have just removed. The corrections you made by hand stay where they are.
settings.enrich.toFiles: Write the tags back into the files
settings.enrich.toFiles.count: Write the tags back into {n} files
settings.enrich.toFiles.count.uno: Write the tags back into {n} file
settings.enrich.legacy.note: Up to 2.3.0 enrichment wrote inside the files: {n} tracks still carry in their tags what it put there, which is why they are not in the count above — what changed them is not in a table of Aether's. That is why “Forget” can say zero on a library that has been enriched for months, and it is not a fault. The next pass takes them over without opening them; {riporta}, instead, puts the previous tags back into the files, and it is the only thing left in Aether that writes inside your music. It will disappear in a future version, once there is nothing left to put back.
settings.theme.title: Theme
settings.theme.label: Light or dark theme
settings.theme.note: «{sistema}» follows {token}, and changes by itself when the computer moves into the evening.
settings.skin.title: Skins
settings.skin.uninstall.active: Uninstall {nome} and go back to the built-in one
settings.tour.title: Guided tour
settings.tour.p1: It puts a spotlight on the real controls, one at a time, and explains them where they are. It starts by itself the first time there is something to listen to; from here you can run it again whenever you like.
settings.eq.title: Equalizer
settings.eq.p1: Ten octave bands, from 31 Hz to 16 kHz: each covers twice the frequencies of the one before, which is how the ear hears them. With bands of equal width in hertz, the first slider alone would hold the bass, the mids and almost every fundamental, and the other nine would share the air that was left.
settings.eq.p2: The filters work inside the audio callback, not before it: that way a slider is heard {mentre} you drag it rather than a fifth of a second later. Raising several bands does not clip — the pre-amplifier measures the peak of the curve and lowers it just enough, automatically.
settings.playback.title: Playback
settings.accent.hint: The accent and its variants take their color from the record that is playing, trimmed in OKLCH so it holds contrast on every surface of the theme. Text never follows the cover, and a black-and-white record changes nothing.
settings.accent.blocked: This skin declares «dynamicAccent: false»: that is a choice by whoever made it, and it wins over this preference — a skin can be built around its accent.
settings.accent.tokens: In this skin, {quanti} tokens declare a source from the cover: they follow the accent on their own, because the compiler writes them as {var}.
settings.accent.tokens.uno: In this skin, {quanti} token declares a source from the cover: it follows the accent on its own, because the compiler writes it as {var}.
settings.replaygain.label: Normalize the volume (ReplayGain)
settings.replaygain.hint: Records that carry the tag are brought to the same perceived volume. “Normal” uses the reference the tag was measured against; “low” sits five decibels below it, for night-time and headphones; “high” is the level the streaming platforms use, and it is why a local library seems to play quieter than they do. A track without the tag is left alone: nothing is measured here, what is written is respected.
settings.sleep.title: Sleep timer
settings.sleep.hint: The music pauses itself when the time is up, and the position stays where it was: it picks up from there. “End of track” cuts nothing short — it simply does not queue up the next one.
settings.autoplay.toggle: Keep going when the queue ends
settings.autoplay.hint: When the last track ends, Aether picks another one from your library instead of stopping: the rest of the record first, then the same artist, then something in the same genre you have not played for a month. It asks no service anything — the choice comes out of your own library. With “repeat all” or “repeat one” it never comes into play, because the queue already has a next.
settings.entry.autoplay: Keep going when the queue ends
settings.output.title: Audio output
settings.output.hint: The list keeps itself up to date: plug headphones in or out and Aether notices within a couple of seconds, moves there by itself and picks up where it left off. Pick a specific card and the sound stays on it even when the system changes its own default — that is how you avoid the music jumping to the speakers when you unplug your headphones.
settings.output.latency.title: Output latency
settings.output.latency.hint: Aether measures the sound card's own buffer, but it cannot see the rest of the chain: the Windows mixer, the driver, the converter, and on a Bluetooth output the radio — which on its own is worth more than all the rest. If the lyrics light up before the voice, raise it; if they arrive late, go below zero. It does not change the sound and it does not move the transition between two tracks: it only moves the point Aether says it is playing.
settings.crossfade.title: Crossfade
settings.crossfade.hint: A track fades into the next one instead of ending and starting again. The curve holds constant energy, so perceived loudness stays put across the overlap: two straight ramps would leave a dip in the middle.
settings.crossfade.gapless: While this is on, sample-exact transitions are gone — including between two tracks of the same record, even the ones written to run together. Set it back to zero to get them back.
settings.spectrum.title: Spectrum
settings.spectrum.toggle.hint: Now Playing opens with the spectrum already running, instead of the cover alone. You can still turn it on and off from the button up top, and whatever you choose there is written back here.
settings.spectrum.quality.label: What the scene is allowed to cost
settings.spectrum.quality.hint: “Automatic” watches how long this computer takes to draw a frame and adjusts itself: it steps down when the scene cannot keep up, and back up when there is room. “High” lets it do everything it knows how to do; “Low” keeps the fan quiet and the battery going. It is the one choice on this card that does not travel in a profile: it describes this computer, not your taste.
settings.spectrum.bars.where: How many bars to draw is chosen while looking at them, not from here: the control sits at the bottom left of the scene, and appears when you hover it or reach it with the tab key.
settings.fileFormat.hint: Under the transport controls, in Now Playing and full screen: format, sample rate, channels and bitrate. It describes the file, not the output — if the sound card resamples, the line stays the same.
settings.shortcuts.title: Keyboard shortcuts
settings.zoom.title: Zoom
settings.zoom.p1: Enlarges the whole interface, not just the text: rows, covers, controls. Enlarging takes room away exactly as narrowing the window does, so past a point the player bar starts withdrawing what it can.
settings.motion.title: Motion and access
settings.motion.p1: Motion is declared by the skin ({token}), and this one says {livello}. If you have turned animation off in the operating system, that choice wins over this one — always, and it is not configurable: an accessibility preference a skin can override is not a preference.
settings.motion.p2: The same rules apply to {layout}: floating or docked player, narrow or open sidebar, comfortable or compact density. They are four fields the format has always accepted and that until today nobody read.
settings.motion.pref.why: From here you can only reduce. A “more” level would contradict the sentence above: an accessibility preference something can override is not a preference.
settings.cloud.title: Backup to Drive
settings.cloud.p1: It saves to Google Drive what a scan {non} rebuild: plays, ratings, favorites, playlists, watched folders, skins and Studio drafts. Not the audio files, not the covers — those find their own way back.
settings.cloud.p2: They land in a private application folder: invisible in Drive, unreadable by any other app, and deleted when you remove Aether's data from your account.
settings.cloud.noCreds: This copy of Aether was built without Google credentials, so the backup cannot start. You can put your own below.
settings.cloud.toggle.hint: One pass every quarter of an hour, and after every change. Only what changed is uploaded.
settings.cloud.browser: Consent is given in the {browser}, not in here: an application window that can draw Google's page is exactly the shape a phishing attempt has.
settings.creds.title: Google credentials
settings.creds.note: Enter the client id and client secret provided by the developer, or create a new pair in the Google Console.
settings.creds.clear: Confirming with both fields empty removes the saved credentials.
settings.creds.step1: Open {console} and create a project. The name does not matter.
settings.creds.step2: {dove}: look for {api} and press «Enable». Without this step consent succeeds and the first request does not.
settings.creds.step3: {dove}: type {tipo}, fill in the required fields, and at the end press {pubblica}. Staying in «Testing» makes the permissions expire after seven days and the backup stops silently.
settings.creds.step3.where: APIs and services › OAuth consent screen
settings.creds.step4: Among the scopes, {scope} is enough: Aether writes only in the application's private folder and does not even see the rest of your Drive.
settings.creds.step5: {dove}, type {tipo}. Not «Web application»: that one demands a redirect address which does not exist here.
settings.creds.step5.where: Credentials › Create credentials › OAuth client ID
settings.creds.step6: Copy the {id} and the {secret}, paste them above and press «Use these».
settings.creds.keyring: The secret goes into the system keyring, not into the library database, and never leaves this computer: it is there to obtain permissions from Google, and nothing else.
settings.sync.title: Sync between devices
settings.sync.p1: It keeps plays, ratings, favorites, resume points and playlist order in line across every computer and phone you use Aether on. {senza}: each device writes its own file, nobody touches anyone else's, and whoever reads puts them together.
settings.sync.p2: {nonBackup} A backup is a photograph with a single author: turned on for two computers, the last one to save covers the earlier one. Here instead the documents {fondono} — five plays on the laptop and three on the phone make eight, not five; rating and heart go to the more recent; a playlist's order is reconciled.
settings.sync.p3: The backup answers «I lost it», the sync answers «I use both», and they can be on together. This one moreover does not ask for Google: a folder that all the devices can see is enough.
settings.sync.toggle.hint: One pass every five minutes, and after every change. On a library that has not moved it writes nothing.
settings.sync.needStore: Choose where to put the documents first
settings.sync.folder.note: Any folder all your devices can see: Syncthing, Dropbox, OneDrive, iCloud Drive, or a USB stick. Aether writes a {sotto} subfolder inside it and touches nothing else.
settings.sync.drive.note: The documents land in the same private folder as the backup: invisible in Drive, unreadable by any other app.
settings.sync.drive.needAccount: Connect a Google account first, from the Backup to Drive section.
settings.sync.devices.note: A new device that shows up in the folder is {ignoto} until you accept it. Giving it a name is how you accept it: from then on you know who the plays you see appearing come from.
settings.sync.forget.note: Forgetting a device {non} delete the plays it has already brought: those were real plays, and removing them would mean that giving up a phone rewrites the library's history.
settings.legacy.title: From the previous version
settings.legacy.note: It brings plays, ratings, favorites, history and playlists over from 1.0.0. The old database is opened {sola} and is never touched: these are the only things a scan cannot rebuild.
settings.import.title: Where the music comes from
settings.import.link.hint: A track, an album or a collection from {a} or {b}. No account, no key: Aether reads what is inside, looks in the library for what you already have, and takes the rest when the license allows it.
settings.import.archive.hint: Playlists, «Liked Songs», saved albums and artists, and years of listening: all at once, instead of thirty links pasted by hand. The zip Spotify hands you on request — it is yours by right, and it stays here.
settings.import.source.download: listen and download, when the individual track's license allows it
settings.import.source.listen: listening only: its terms forbid copying and offline access
settings.import.alt.hint: Concerts, reissues, reinterpretations: the free catalogs are mostly made of these. When it takes one, Aether says so — the «live» pill next to the track. Turned off, the queue is strict and finds far less.
settings.import.how.p1: Only the names are taken from the archive: the tracks you do not have are looked up in the {cataloghi}, and Aether picks the file, preferring the one that carries the author's name and a matching length.
settings.import.how.p2: What it finds, it takes {solo}, and the check happens before any request. What no free catalog has ends up under {daComprare}, with links to the shops where the artist is paid: that is not a fault, it is the honest answer.
settings.import.how.p2.only: only if the license allows it
settings.import.how.p3: The free catalogs do not have the studio versions of the commercial catalog: they have concerts, reissues, reinterpretations. Aether accepts them and {dice} which one it took — the «live» pill next to the track. Anyone rebuilding one exact record turns off «Accept different recordings» above.
settings.import.how.p4: The plays imported from the archive stay {riconoscibili}: they can be removed without touching the real ones.
settings.import.how.p5: The files go into the first watched folder and a scan brings them into the library on its own. What cannot be fetched stays as a list, with everything the source says about it.
settings.queue.empty: Imports are followed in {porta}: the queue keeps going with the screen closed, and the reports reopen from there.
settings.scrobbling.title: Scrobbling
settings.scrobbling.note: what goes out, not what comes in
settings.models.title: AI Models
ia.p1: A language model serves exactly one purpose in Aether: the Skin Studio chat, where you can ask for a skin's colors, spacing and effects to be changed instead of writing them by hand. Until you configure one here, that chat talks to nobody and no request goes out.
ia.p2: Ollama and Bionic run {locali}: what you write does not leave. OpenRouter is an outside service, and with it every message carries the skin document and what you type in the chat — never your library, never your listens.
ia.keyring: The key goes into the system keyring, not into the library database, and never passes through the window: the core reads it an instant before each request.
ia.provider.localNote: It runs on this computer and wants no key: it only has to be running. With Ollama the service just needs to be up; with Bionic you open LM Studio, the Developer tab, and press Start server.
ia.provider.remoteNote: It is an outside service: it wants a key, and what you send it leaves this computer. An address in the clear that is not this machine is refused — such a request would be readable by anyone in between.
ia.name: Name (for you)
ia.tested: {n} models available: the field suggests them now.
ia.tested.none: The service answers, but declares no model. The name can be typed by hand.
ia.test.afterSave: Testing comes after saving: the key lives in the keyring under the profile's name, and testing first would mean passing it through the window for a single request.
settings.data.title: Library and data
settings.data.noMigrations: On the last start the database was already up to date.
settings.data.migrations: On the last start the database was upgraded ({n} steps).
settings.data.fts.missing: FTS5 is not available: search does not work.
settings.profile.title: Aether profile
settings.profile.note: choices and library, not your music files
settings.update.title: Updates
settings.update.note: one request every half hour, and nothing inside it
settings.update.p1: Every half hour Aether asks GitHub whether a newer version is out. It is a short public file — the same one you would see by opening the releases page in a browser — and nothing of yours goes into the request, not even the version you have installed: the comparison happens here, in the program, after the file has been read.
settings.update.p2: When it finds one it says so and stops there. Downloading and installing take a button press: installing means closing Aether, and that is not something to do while you are listening. The installer that arrives is checked against the signature of whoever published it, and if the signature does not match it is not run.
settings.update.toggle.hint: Off, Aether never talks to GitHub. You will have to come here and press “Check now”, or download the installer yourself.
settings.update.unsigned: This copy of Aether was built without signing keys: it could not verify what it downloads, so it does not download.
settings.update.upToDate: You have the latest version: Aether {v}.
settings.diary.hint: When something goes wrong, Aether writes it there: three text files, holding fault codes and nothing else. Your track titles and your library paths never go in, so the file can be attached to a bug report without a second thought.
settings.docs.title: Documents
settings.docs.hint: They open in the system browser, on the repository, so what you read is the current version and not the one this executable was built from. The same copies also sit in the install folder.
settings.docs.terms: What you may do with the music
settings.background.title: Closing and background
settings.background.note: what the X in the corner does
settings.background.p1: On, the close button does not quit Aether: it hides the window and lets the music play. Everything stays where it was — the queue, the point in the track, the volume — and an icon appears in the notification area, next to the clock. A click reopens the window; right-click for «Quit», which really does quit.
settings.background.p2: The minimize button is unchanged: whoever presses it already knows where to find the window again, on the taskbar. And if the system were to refuse the icon, the X goes back to closing — a hidden window you cannot come back to would be worse than the other way round.
settings.background.toggle: The X hides instead of closing
settings.background.toggle.hint: Off, the close button quits Aether the way it always has.
update.later.hint: Hides the notice until Aether starts again
update.skip.hint: Don't offer this version again: the notice comes back with the next one
cmd.alterna.title: Pause and resume
cmd.alterna.hint: Stops whatever is playing, or picks it up where it was.
cmd.cerca.title: Search
cmd.cerca.hint: Puts the cursor in the search field, going back to the library if need be.
cmd.avanti.title: Forward five seconds
cmd.avanti.hint: Moves the position within the track, without leaving it.
cmd.indietro.title: Back five seconds
cmd.inRiproduzione.title: Open «Now playing»
cmd.inRiproduzione.hint: The track full screen, and again to close it.
cmd.schermoIntero.title: Full-screen window
cmd.schermoIntero.hint: Clears the rest of the desktop away, and again to go back to a window.
cmd.ingrandisci.title: Enlarge the interface
cmd.ingrandisci.hint: One step bigger, up to twice the size.
cmd.rimpicciolisci.title: Shrink the interface
cmd.rimpicciolisci.hint: One step smaller, down to ninety per cent.
cmd.zoomNormale.title: Default size
cmd.zoomNormale.hint: Puts the interface back as it was, from any step.
cmd.importazioni.title: Open «Imports»
cmd.importazioni.hint: The queue that downloads, and the reports of imports already made.
cmd.incollaLink.title: Paste a link
cmd.incollaLink.hint: The dialog that reads a link from a free catalog, from any page.
shortcuts.intro: Press {assegna} and then whichever key you want. A command can have more than one. {esc} cannot be reassigned: it is the way out of every dialog and every field, and a way out that can be locked is not a way out.
shortcuts.contested: {tasto} is also assigned to another command
shortcuts.clash: The same key for several commands
shortcuts.clash.tail: . While it stays this way the first in this list wins — that is not random, but it is almost certainly not what you meant.
shortcuts.forbidden.escape: Escape closes whatever is open, always: it is the emergency exit.
shortcuts.forbidden.tab: Tab moves the focus: it is what keyboard navigation runs on.
eq.reset.title: Bring every band back to zero
eq.save.name: Name for the curve…
eq.delete.title: Delete
profile.nothingChanged: The profile changed nothing: everything was already like this.
profile.note: A single file with your choices and your library — theme, skin, equalizer, shortcuts, folders, listens, ratings, playlists, lyrics and cover art — to reopen on another computer or after a reinstall. It {non} hold your music files, nor the tokens of connected services: those live in the system keyring and do not leave it.
profile.undo: Put it back as it was
profile.undo.note: Restores the settings and the skin from the copy written before the import. Listens, playlists and lyrics stay: they were added, not replaced.
profile.undone: Settings and skin put back as they were.
profile.exported.title: What went out
profile.brings.listens.uno: {n} track with a new play count
profile.heavy: More than half a gigabyte: it fits on a USB stick, but better to know before copying it.
profile.leftHere: Left behind: {chiavi}. These are keys that identify {questo} computer or that name rows of {questa} library — on another machine they would say wrong things rather than nothing.
profile.otherLibrary.merging: This profile comes from a different library, and you said it is yours: listens, ratings and playlists will be joined to the tracks here with the same title, artist and album.
profile.mergeAnyway: It's my library: merge anyway (for example if you exported a profile from this computer before importing the old one)
profile.otherLibrary: This profile comes from a different library. Settings, covers and skins still apply; listens, ratings and playlists do not, because over there the tracks are other tracks, and attaching them here would credit you with listens you never made.
profile.remap.note: These folders do not exist on this computer. Write where they are now and the track paths will follow — but only those whose file is actually found.
profile.noChanges: Nothing would change: this computer's settings already match the file.
profile.remap.rewritten: {n} track paths will follow the new folder.
profile.remap.rewritten.uno: {n} track path will follow the new folder.
profile.remap.missing: {n} tracks are not found under the new folder: their row stays as it is, because an old path tells the truth about where it was, and a new one would lie about where it is.
profile.remap.missing.uno: {n} track is not found under the new folder: its row stays as it is, because an old path tells the truth about where it was, and a new one would lie about where it is.
profile.remap.already: {n} tracks are already there under the new folder, with their own history: they are not overwritten.
profile.remap.already.uno: {n} track is already there under the new folder, with its own history: it is not overwritten.
profile.missingPaths: {titolo}: {percorsi}. They are written anyway — a folder can be on a drive that is unplugged now and plugged in tomorrow — but the scan will find nothing until they are there.
profile.missingPaths.title: These paths do not exist on this computer
profile.unknownKeys: Keys this version does not carry, and that will be ignored: {chiavi}.
profile.whenApplied: Theme, skin and shortcuts show up right away. Volume, equalizer and normalization are read by the engine when it opens: those change at the next start.
profile.additive: Listens, playlists, lyrics and covers are added to what you have: nothing is removed. That is also why they cannot be undone — undo restores the settings and the skin, not the history.
restore.done.title: Restore finished
restore.missing.note: This happens when a save was interrupted between the metadata and the packages. The rest was restored: the next save sends them back up.
restore.foldersBack: Some watched folders came back. {scansiona}: the tracks that were inside come back into the library and find their statistics again.
restore.noBackup: There is no backup on Drive yet. Connect an account from Settings and let one save go through.
restore.plan.empty: There is nothing to restore: what is in the backup is already here.
restore.absent: {n} tracks from the backup have no file here
restore.absent.note: The restore {non}: a row with no file cannot be opened, and the next scan would remove it. They are listed so you know what to go looking for. The names are in the normalized form of the tags.
restore.playlist.smart: , automatic: it receives the rules, not the tracks
restore.keptAsIs: Those that are already here are left alone: {skin} skins and {bozze} drafts stay as they are.
restore.shownAllUpdated: Showing the first {quanti} of {totale}. All of them will be updated.
account.empty.hint: There were none in here: there is nothing to import.
account.title: Your Spotify account
account.already.note: They stay distinguishable from the real ones, and can be removed. The play counts, however, {non}: that number is the one thing in the library that cannot be rebuilt, and a feature that lowers it will sooner or later lower it when it should not have.
account.otherArchive: There is no listening history in here. Spotify sends it in a separate archive, «Extended streaming history», which arrives up to thirty days after the other one.
account.unreadable: {n} files in the archive would not open. The rest was read anyway.
account.nothing: There is nothing to import in here. If it is an archive, it may be the other of the two Spotify sends: look for the one containing {a} or {b}.
account.pick.playlists.hint: {n} tracks in all. One playlist here for each one there; reimporting replaces rather than appends.
account.pick.liked.hint: They become favorites here. Not a playlist: Aether already has its own place for favorites.
account.pick.albums.hint: They attach the Spotify identifier to records you already have, so editions of the same album merge.
account.pick.artists.hint: Only for the ones you already have in the library: the others would vanish at the first scan.
account.pick.history.hint: They stay marked as imported, and can be removed. Only those played for at least half the track count, the same rule as when Aether is playing.
account.toLike.note: the ones already marked are not counted
account.skipped: left out: {doppioni} duplicates, {brevi} too short, {fuori} not in the library
account.rejected: {n} playlists would be skipped. The others come in anyway.
archive.step1: Open {sito} and scroll down to «Download your data».
archive.step2: Tick {dati} and {cronologia}, then confirm from the email you receive.
archive.step2.warn: They are two different archives that arrive at different times: the first within a few days, the second within thirty. Aether opens one at a time, and whatever is missing simply stays empty.
archive.step3: When it arrives, come back here and open it. There is no need to unzip it: the zip is fine as it is.
archive.intro: Aether reads the archive Spotify hands you on request: your playlists, your favorites, your albums, and your listening history {intero}. It asks for no consent and never talks to Spotify: the file is yours, and it stays here.
archive.askNow: It is worth asking for it {adesso}: it takes days to arrive, and until then there is nothing to wait for in front of this screen.
legacy.unmatched: {n} tracks from the old database are not in the library
legacy.unmatched.note: Their statistics stay behind. Usually this means the files were moved or deleted: a scan of the right folders, then back here, gets them.
link.allDown: Nobody is responding: it is almost always this computer, not them. Check the connection.
link.someUp: The ones that respond are working: the problem is in the link, or in this item. An Internet Archive item can exist and have restricted access — in that case you listen on the site and do not take it away, and Aether respects that instead of trying.
link.title: Import from a catalog
link.intro: Paste the link of a track, an album or a collection from a free catalog. No account and no key needed: Aether reads what is inside, looks in the library for the tracks you already have, and {solo}.
link.intro.only: takes only what the license allows to be taken
link.label: Link
link.allDownloadable: All downloadable: the license allows it.
link.noneDownloadable: {nessuno}: here you listen, you do not take away. The entries go under «To buy».
link.noneDownloadable.head: None downloadable
link.someDownloadable: {quanti} of {totale} can be downloaded; the others can only be listened to.
link.degraded: Only the {titolo} and the {copertina} came back for this link: the track list did not arrive. Importing it now would create an empty playlist. It could be the catalog that changed something, or a bad moment on the network.
link.degraded.title: title
link.truncated: {fonte} declares {attesi} but sent {letti}. Importing now, the {mancanti} that are missing would stay out.
link.replaces: — it already exists, and its contents would be replaced
link.smartEscape: Import the tracks without creating the playlist
link.notFound.note: they will be looked for in the free catalogs
link.spotifyIds.note: they merge editions of the same album already in the library
link.missing: {n} tracks are not in the library
link.missing.uno: {n} track is not in the library
link.missing.p1: On confirmation, these are looked up one by one in the free catalogs. The file is already the one in the list above: no other is sought, and it is taken only if its license allows. What no free catalog has ends up under {daComprare}, with links to get it where the artist is paid.
link.missing.p2: If instead the files are already there but in a folder that is not watched, it is worth adding it and running a scan — then coming back here: only what is really missing will be taken.
link.missing.p3: These names are not lost by closing: the report stays under {importazioni} and reopens whenever you want.

scrobble.nothingToQueue: There was nothing to queue: they were all queued or already sent.
scrobble.p1: It sends what you listen to a service that keeps your history. It counts by the same rule as everything else in Aether — {regola}, whichever comes first — so a track skipped after three seconds does not go out, exactly as it does not end up in your «most played».
scrobble.p1.rule: half the track or four minutes
scrobble.p2: Whatever does not go out because there is no network {nonPerde}: it stays in a queue on disk and starts again by itself, even after a shutdown.
scrobble.toggle.on: Turned off, the queue stops filling up: you do not find three days of listens sent all at once when you turn it back on.
scrobble.lb.note: From MetaBrainz, the same people as MusicBrainz. The data is public and downloadable: your history stays yours even if the service closes one day. All it needs is a token, which lives in your account settings.
scrobble.backlog: Send the history you already have too
scrobble.backlog.p1: ListenBrainz is the only one of the two that accepts old listens in bulk: if you imported your history from Spotify, those are years of listening that can become your history on a service that belongs to no platform.
scrobble.backlog.p2: It never sends anything twice: what has already gone out does not go back into the queue. On Last.fm this cannot be done — it refuses listens with an old date and has a daily cap.
scrobble.backlog.only: Only what was imported from Spotify
scrobble.lfm.note: It needs an application registered in your name — Last.fm does not allow one to be shipped inside a program. It takes a minute to create at {sito}, and it gives you a key and a secret to paste here.
scrobble.lfm.needCreds: Paste the key and secret above first
scrobble.lfm.waiting: The Last.fm page is now open in the {browser}. Give consent there, then come back here and press «I authorized it»: Last.fm tells nobody when you are done, so this step has to be done by hand. The permission lasts an hour.

studio.motion.intensity.note: It scales every duration in the sheet, and composes with the system preference instead of overriding it: whoever turned animation off wins over «maximum», always.

skin.token.canvas.scrubber.glow: Glow of the playhead. Flat skins set it to zero.
skin.token.canvas.scrubber.rest: The not-yet-played wave in the scrubber.
skin.token.canvas.viz.ambient: Diffuse light: how much of the face turned away from the light you can see. At 1 the scene is flat and shadowless.
skin.token.canvas.viz.attack: Milliseconds a bar takes to rise. Short: the scene snaps. Long: it moves like a VU meter.
skin.token.canvas.viz.beat: How hard the kick drum pushes the camera. At 0 the scene follows the volume and ignores the beat.
skin.token.canvas.viz.depth: How far back the past goes: the depth of the room, that is, how much history you see.
skin.token.canvas.viz.eye: The height you watch from: at 0 you are on the floor, at 2 you look down on the row.
skin.token.canvas.viz.fill: How much of its slice a bar takes up: towards 1 the bars touch, towards 0.1 they become needles.
skin.token.canvas.viz.floor: Noise floor in decibels: how quiet a sound must be to draw nothing. Towards −24 only the hits are left.
skin.token.canvas.viz.glow: How brightly the crest lights up: at 0 the bar is a single colour, at 100 the tip is all light.
skin.token.canvas.viz.haze: How deep into the room the past starts fading into the background. High: the history stays sharp all the way back.
skin.token.canvas.viz.height: How tall a bar grows when its band peaks. At 0 it stays a floor that changes colour.
skin.token.canvas.viz.lens: Lens aperture, in degrees. Below 35 the perspective flattens, above 70 it exaggerates.
skin.token.canvas.viz.primary: The colour at the top of the bars: the one read as “the colour” of the scene.
skin.token.canvas.viz.reflection: How much the floor reflects the row. At 0 the reflection is not drawn at all.
skin.token.canvas.viz.release: Milliseconds a bar takes to fall. It is the time that decides whether silence arrives at once or fades.
skin.token.canvas.viz.secondary: The colour at the base of the bars. The further it is from the top one, the more relief the row has.
skin.token.canvas.viz.sway: How much the camera drifts on its own, with no push from the sound. At 0 the viewpoint holds still.
skin.token.canvas.viz.tip: The lit crest on the last stretch of each bar, where the colour turns to light.
skin.token.canvas.viz.width: The width of the room the row stands in: the wider it is, the more the row spreads out and flattens.
skin.token.color.accent: Primary accent. It can follow the cover being played.
skin.token.color.accent.like: Fill of the heart. Nothing takes it to red, its only red.
skin.token.color.accent.soft: Accent at low opacity: backgrounds of active states.
skin.token.color.ambient.1: First glow of the ambient backdrop.
skin.token.color.ambient.2: Second glow of the ambient backdrop.
skin.token.color.hairline: The one-pixel lines that separate the surfaces.
skin.token.color.hero: Tint of the heroes, usually derived from the cover.
skin.token.color.success: Confirmations and operations that went through.
skin.token.color.surface.0: The ground of the application. It is also the cold-start color.
skin.token.color.text.2: Secondary text. The contrast check looks mostly at this one.
skin.token.color.text.3: Tertiary text, at the edge of legibility: it needs checking.
skin.token.color.warning: Warnings that do not block the operation.
skin.token.depth.edge: How much the light edge along the top of surfaces stands out.
skin.token.depth.inset: How deep tracks, grooves and fields sink.
skin.token.depth.lift: How much the top of a surface lightens.
skin.token.depth.sheen: How far down the light gradient reaches before it runs out.
skin.token.font.display: Display face: large titles, numbers, eyebrows.
skin.token.motion.ease.outExpo: Main exit curve. The route transitions use it too.
skin.token.radius.inner: How much of the cards' radius the inner containers take.
skin.token.radius.panel: Radius of the panels. Cyberpunk takes it to 4px, and that is half its identity.
skin.token.radius.tiny: How much of it the small details take: pills, boxes, handles.
skin.token.shadow.player: Elevation of the floating player, with its inner hairline.
skin.token.space.1: The narrowest step: inside a chip, between an icon and its label.
skin.token.space.2: Between elements side by side in the same row.
skin.token.space.3: The base step: inside the cards, between the rows of a list.
skin.token.space.4: Between the blocks of a page.
skin.token.space.5: Between the large sections, and at the edges of the screens.
